introH2: 🏖️ What is Kamala Beach like, and which part should you stay in?
introHtml: If Patong is Phuket's loudest beach, Kamala — the very next bay north — is its calm opposite in almost every way. A gentle 2-kilometre curve of sand with a Muslim fishing village still living behind it, shallow water that's easy for a swim, European families who settle in for a month at a time in high season, and evenings quiet enough to hear the waves · At the southern headland the coast road climbs into Millionaire's Mile, the cliffside stretch where luxury villas and sea-view hotels hang above the water with front-row sunset views, and on the jungle hillside above the village sits the pool-villa resort the whole world knows from one photo of a bird's-nest villa · That mix means Kamala has stays from a thousand baht a night to five figures, each one a genuinely different experience — book the wrong zone and the whole mood of your trip changes: you wanted to walk barefoot to the sand but ended up on a hill that needs a car, or brought a toddler to an adults-preferred hotel · This guide gathers 7 Kamala Beach hotels we've reviewed in depth, covering every budget — all built from reading real guest reviews, with the good and the honest caveats spelled out, prices compared across 3 booking sites, and direct links to book
mrtHtml: Phuket has no rail transit — you'll get around by rental car, Grab, or hotel transfer · Kamala sits on the island's west coast, about 45 minutes–1 hour from Phuket Airport (HKT) and 15–20 minutes over the hill from Patong · The zones in this guide: On the beach — on the sand or across the road from it, walkable to village restaurants and markets (InterContinental, Sunwing, Layalina) · In Kamala village — 150–300 m inland, a 2–3 minute walk to the sand, noticeably cheaper (PapaCrab, Glam Habitat) · Southern hillside / Millionaire's Mile — sea views from above, very quiet, but the slope means driving (Cape Sienna) · Jungle hillside above the village — green and private, ~10 minutes from the beach with a resort shuttle (Keemala) · After dark Kamala is far quieter than Patong; if nightlife matters, budget for taxis over the hill

entries.addr: 10/88 Moo 6, Nakasud Road, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: If you had to name one Kamala stay people recognise from a single photo, it's Keemala — a 5-star resort of 38 pool villas on the rainforest hillside above Kamala village, its four villa styles drawn from the legends of four fictional clans: earthy Clay Cottages, canvas Tent Villas, Tree Houses with cocoon-shaped beds, and the Bird's Nest villas that became modern Phuket's postcard image. Every villa has its own pool, and the score — 9.2 from 771 reviews — is the highest in this list · Real guests keep saying the magic isn't just the villa shapes: it's waking up inside the tree canopy with birdsong and jungle all around, plus Mala Spa and a wellness-driven kitchen taken seriously enough that some people come for the spa alone · The honest caveats: it's not on the beach — the resort shuttle takes about 10 minutes down to Kamala sand — the paths inside are steep with plenty of steps, mosquitoes come with the jungle, and peak-season rates climb high enough that some reviews question the value. Book low season and the value equation improves clearly · Best for honeymooners, design lovers, and wellness travellers who want a stay they'll still be talking about years later
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Each villa clan feels very different — pick the Bird's Nest for views and the iconic look, the Tent Villa to hear the jungle at its clearest, or the Clay Cottage for the gentlest price · May–October rates drop substantially · Pack mosquito spray and comfortable walking shoes, because the resort paths are steep
pros: 9.2 — the highest score in this list · villa designs from 4 clan legends, like nowhere else
Private pool in every villa, deeply private — honeymoon territory
Mala Spa and wellness dining praised consistently in reviews
Genuinely quiet rainforest setting above Kamala — you wake up in the tree canopy
cons: Not on the beach — resort shuttle ~10 minutes down to Kamala sand
Steep paths and lots of steps inside the resort · jungle mosquitoes are part of the deal
Peak-season rates run high — several reviews suggest booking low season (from reviews)

entries.name: InterContinental Phuket Resort
entries.badge: 🌊 Best beachfront resort in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 South Kamala Beach · directly on the sand · quietest stretch of the bay
entries.storyHtml: If your one non-negotiable is a real beachfront — walking from your room onto the sand without crossing a road — InterContinental Phuket Resort is Kamala's number one. A 5-star resort of 221 rooms and villas on the southern end of Kamala Beach, the quietest, shadiest stretch of the bay under a line of casuarina trees that many reviewers describe as feeling like a private beach. It scores 9.1 from 1,220 reviews and holds Michelin 2 Keys 2026, the Michelin Guide's hotel-side award · Inside there are 5 pools and 7 restaurants and bars, including Jaras, a Thai restaurant listed in the Michelin Guide. Real reviews consistently praise the large, immaculately clean rooms — the freestanding tub and balcony in the Classic rooms get frequent mentions — and service that gets warm words from check-in to check-out · The honest caveats from guest reviews: total spend runs high once resort food and drinks are counted, entry-level rooms sit in the Mountain Wing with no sea view (you'll need an Ocean View room or villa for that), and Kamala goes quiet after dark — nightlife means a taxi to Patong · Best for travellers who plan to spend most of their time inside the resort and want a no-surprises 5-star right on the sand
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry-level Classic rooms face the hills — upgrade to Premium Club Ocean View for the sea and Club InterContinental lounge access, well worth it if you enjoy a sunset cocktail hour · Book a table at Jaras ahead of time for a special dinner · And budget properly for resort dining, since prices match the luxury tier
pros: Directly on south Kamala Beach — the quietest, shadiest stretch of the bay
Michelin 2 Keys 2026 + Jaras restaurant in the Michelin Guide
Large, immaculately clean rooms and consistently praised service (from reviews)
5 pools and 7 restaurants & bars — you can happily never leave
cons: Total costs run high, for both rooms and resort dining
Entry-level rooms are in the Mountain Wing with no sea view — views cost more
Kamala is quiet after dark; nightlife means a ride to Patong (from reviews)

entries.name: Sunwing Kamala Beach
entries.badge: 👨‍👩‍👧 Best family resort in this list
entries.mrtTag: 📍 On Kamala Beach, central–north section · straight onto the sand
entries.storyHtml: If this trip is measured by your kids' smiles, Sunwing Kamala Beach is the resort European families have been rebooking for decades — a 4-star, 317-room family resort on the central–north section of Kamala Beach, with the sand right off the property. It scores 8.8 from 1,226 reviews · The heart of the place is a system built entirely around children: 8 pools with water slides and the Lollo & Bernie kids club with real activity leaders, family shows several nights a week, and studio rooms from 44 sqm up — every one with a kitchenette, fridge and microwave for warming milk or late-night meals. Kids under 12 stay free, which visibly lightens the family budget, and the Happy Baby Studios come pre-stocked with a cot, high chair, stroller and baby bath · Real reviews praise how little planning it all takes — the kids are entertained all day and the parents actually get a holiday · The honest caveats: children's noise carries across the resort all day, so couples wanting quiet should pick elsewhere in this list; the buildings are 15+ years old and show their age in places; Wi-Fi is weak; and peak-season rates multiply several times over during the European family season
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With a baby or toddler, look at the ground-floor Happy Baby Studios with full baby kit and a lockable fenced terrace · Families with teens should pick the Two-Bedroom Family Suite, where two 12–17-year-olds stay free · And book May–October, when rates drop clearly from the high-season peak
pros: 8 pools with slides + a kids club with real activity leaders — children entertained all day
On Kamala Beach with the sand right there · kitchenette in every room
Kids under 12 stay free — a real difference to the family budget
Big review base of 1,226 · European families rebook year after year
cons: Children's noise carries across the resort — not for couples seeking quiet
Buildings are 15+ years old and show it in places · weak Wi-Fi (from reviews)
Peak-season rates multiply several times over in the European family season

entries.storyHtml: On the hillside at Kamala's southern end, where the coast road climbs into Millionaire's Mile, one hotel makes a single promise with no exceptions — at Cape Sienna Phuket Gourmet Hotel & Villas, all 146 rooms face the sea with a private balcony. No garden-view or hill-view rooms to gamble on. It scores 8.4 from 1,834 reviews, the biggest review base in this list · The word Gourmet in the name is earned: Plum steakhouse takes its beef seriously, and the Vanilla Sky rooftop bar with its 180-degree sea view has become the neighbourhood's sunset spot, joined by a clifftop infinity pool with camera angles that hotels twice the price would envy. The mood is adults-preferred and calm — young children can't stay during high season — which makes it a couples' favourite · Real reviews frame it simply: this is the kind of view a beachfront resort can't give you, at low-season prices that are surprisingly reachable · The honest caveats: it sits on a hill, not on the beach — reaching Kamala sand means a steep walk or a short drive — there are plenty of stairs inside, and some rooms are showing their age · Best for couples and honeymooners who put views and good meals at the top of the list
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Sea View Deluxe rooms on higher floors get a more open sea view than the Studios for not much more · For a private soak, pick the Jacuzzi Junior Suite with its balcony tub · Reserve a Vanilla Sky table for sunset ahead of time — people come from outside the hotel for it · And travelling with young children, check the seasonal child policy before booking
pros: Sea view and private balcony in every single room — nothing to gamble on
Plum steakhouse + Vanilla Sky rooftop bar, both taken seriously (from reviews)
Clifftop infinity pool — the neighbourhood's sunset viewpoint
Adults-preferred calm, made for couples · reachable low-season prices
cons: Not on the beach — a steep walk or short drive down to the sand
Lots of stairs; hard work for anyone with mobility issues · some rooms showing age (from reviews)
Families with young children can't stay during high season

entries.storyHtml: In an era when the word beachfront gets stretched, Layalina Hotel is the real thing you can measure in footsteps — a boutique hotel of just 15 rooms on Kamala's beach road, its building touching the shore, less than 20 metres from door to sand. It scores 8.6 from 470 reviews and starts around ฿2,000/night — several times cheaper than most on-the-sand stays in Phuket · What real reviewers mention most is the sunset from the room balconies, especially the Duplex rooms with a private rooftop deck and sun loungers where you can watch the sky change colour without sharing the view with anyone. Add breakfast that can be served to your balcony and a small team that gets to know guests by name · The honest caveats from reviews: the pool is small — closer to a jacuzzi than a swimming pool — the entrance is a local village soi, the canal in front carries a smell in some seasons, and the hotel doesn't sell alcohol (you may bring your own for private enjoyment), in keeping with Kamala's Muslim community · Best for couples and travellers who want to wake up to the sea from bed for a four-digit price, and don't need big-resort facilities
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Duplex Private Heaven Rooftop is the room guests rebook most — the private roof deck earns its price difference · Cocktail-by-the-sea people should plan on the beach bars nearby, since the hotel doesn't sell alcohol · And book ahead in high season, because there are only 15 rooms
pros: The building touches the Kamala sand — under 20 metres from door to sea
Sunset views from the room balconies · Duplex rooms have a private roof deck
Breakfast served to your balcony · staff know guests by name (from reviews)
A four-digit price for a true on-the-sand stay — rare in Phuket
cons: The pool is tiny — more jacuzzi than swimming pool
Village-soi entrance · the canal out front smells in some seasons (from reviews)
No alcohol sold at the hotel, in keeping with the local Muslim community

entries.addr: 93/5 Moo 3, Rimhad Road, Kamala, Kathu, Phuket
entries.storyHtml: A 9.0 score from 282 reviews at around ฿1,500/night is not a combination you see often, and behind the number at PapaCrab Boutique Guesthouse is a very simple formula — a 10-room guesthouse in the middle of Kamala village, about 200 metres and a 2–3 minute walk from the sand, where Charly the owner runs everything personally, every day: answering messages before you arrive, pointing you to the village's best kitchens, and helping plan your days like a friend who happens to live in Phuket · Real reviews praise the cleanliness so consistently it has become the house signature; every room has a private balcony or terrace, fridge, kettle and hot water, and there's a 2-bedroom apartment with a full kitchen for longer stays plus a 3-bedroom private-pool villa for groups · The honest caveats to know before booking: this is a 2.5-star guesthouse — the main house has no pool and no on-site breakfast (the village cafés are all walkable), rooms aren't large, and with only 10 rooms, high-season dates tend to be booked out well ahead · Best for budget travellers who value cleanliness, a beach-walkable location and an owner's personal care over in-house facilities
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for an inner room away from the village road if you want the quietest sleep · Groups and long-stayers should look at the 2-bedroom apartment with its full kitchen — cheaper than booking two rooms · And plan ahead for November–March, since there are only 10 rooms
pros: A 9.0 score — among the highest in this list — at the group's lightest prices
Owner-run daily; trip-planning help like a friend in Phuket (from reviews)
Cleanliness praised in review after review · private balcony or terrace on every room
2–3 minute walk to the beach · apartment and private-pool villa options too
cons: No pool at the main guesthouse and no on-site breakfast
Rooms aren't large — true to its 2.5-star guesthouse tier
Only 10 rooms, so high-season dates book out well ahead (from reviews)

entries.type: Pool Suite Hotel 3★ · private pool in every room
entries.name: Glam Habitat
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Kamala · 2 min walk to the beach (~150 m)
entries.storyHtml: The most improbable-sounding line in this list happens to be true — at Glam Habitat, a hotel of 27 suites and 3 villas in central Kamala, every room comes with its own private pool, from about ฿1,400/night in low season, a spec that normally costs several times more anywhere in Phuket. It scores 8.8 from 82 reviews · The entry One-Bedroom Pool Suite runs about 80 sqm in an apartment style with a separate living room and an open kitchen you can genuinely cook in, the beach is about 150 metres away on foot, and up on the roof there's a sea-view infinity pool for sunset on top of the one in your room · Real reviews praise the space-for-money ratio, the privacy of an in-room pool, and caring staff · The honest caveats to keep in mind: the review base is still small at 82 — the smallest in this list, and the reason we rank it seventh despite the strong score — street-facing rooms hear traffic, some fittings are showing their age, check-in requires a cash deposit, and peak-season prices jump well above the low-season rate · Best for couples and groups of friends who want a pool they don't share with anyone at a four-digit price, and don't mind the absence of a big brand name or box-fresh fittings
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for an inner room away from the road if you're a light sleeper · Groups of 4–6 should look at the Two-Bedroom Pool Suite or the 3-bedroom villa — cheaper per person than booking separately · Bring cash for the check-in deposit · And book low season (May–October) for the headline starting rates
pros: A private pool in every room at four-digit prices — genuinely hard to find
Rooms from ~80 sqm, apartment-style with a real kitchen
2-minute walk to Kamala Beach · rooftop sea-view infinity pool
Caring staff and strong space-for-money value (from reviews)
cons: Small review base of 82 — the smallest here, and why it ranks 7th despite the score
Street-facing rooms hear traffic · some fittings showing age (from reviews)
Cash deposit at check-in · peak-season prices jump well above low season

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard-room range outside peak dates and may change by date and season — always check live prices and compare all 3 sites before booking · Scores and highlights in this guide come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms; we did not stay as guests · Phuket's high season (November–April) brings clearly higher rates, and the small properties — Layalina and PapaCrab — tend to fill first, so plan ahead · Kamala is a quiet neighbourhood where restaurants close earlier than Patong; getting around means a rental car or Grab · The hillside stays (Keemala, Cape Sienna) involve steep paths and stairs, hard work for anyone with mobility issues · A guide by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about Kamala Beach hotels in Phuket

faq.q: ❓ What is the best hotel on Kamala Beach?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget · Going by score alone, Keemala at 9.2 — the rainforest pool-villa resort — leads the list · If it must be a true beachfront, InterContinental Phuket Resort at 9.1 with Michelin 2 Keys is Kamala's best resort on the sand · For families, Sunwing Kamala Beach brings 8 pools and a full kids club · On a budget, PapaCrab scores 9.0 at around ฿1,500 a night

faq.q: ❓ How much do Kamala Beach hotels cost?
faq.a: The stays in this guide start at roughly ฿1,400–12,000 per night · At the light end: Glam Habitat from ฿1,400 (with a private pool in every room) and PapaCrab from ฿1,500 · Mid-range: Layalina ฿2,000, Sunwing ฿2,500 and Cape Sienna ฿2,900 · At the luxury end: InterContinental from ฿7,500 and Keemala from ฿12,000 · All are approximate off-peak starting rates; high season (November–April) runs clearly higher

faq.q: ❓ How is Kamala different from Patong — and who is it for?
faq.a: Kamala is the next bay north of Patong, 15–20 minutes over the hill, but the mood is a different world — Kamala is calm, built around a Muslim fishing village, quiet after dark, with shallow swimmable water and European families who stay for a month at a time, while Patong is the island's nightlife engine · Kamala suits families, couples and anyone who actually wants to rest · If you plan on going out every night, staying in Patong is easier — or stay in Kamala and taxi over the hill when the mood strikes

faq.q: ❓ Which Kamala Beach hotel is best for families?
faq.a: The most family-built of all is Sunwing Kamala Beach ฿2,500 — 8 pools with slides, the staffed Lollo & Bernie kids club, kitchenettes in every room and kids under 12 staying free · Larger families and groups should look at Glam Habitat with 2-bedroom suites and 3–4-bedroom private-pool villas, or PapaCrab's 2-bedroom apartment with a full kitchen · Note that Cape Sienna is adults-preferred and doesn't take young children in high season

faq.q: ❓ What is Millionaire's Mile — and which Kamala zone should I stay in?
faq.a: Millionaire's Mile is the clifftop road at Kamala's southern end, running toward Laem Singh, where luxury villas and sea-view hotels cling to the hillside with front-row sunset views — Cape Sienna sits at the start of it · Picking a zone: to walk barefoot to the sand, stay on the beach (InterContinental, Sunwing, Layalina) · on a budget, stay in the village 2–3 minutes' walk away (PapaCrab, Glam Habitat) · for views from above, the southern hillside (Cape Sienna) · for privacy in nature, the jungle hillside above the village (Keemala)

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book — and how do I get to Kamala?
faq.a: In Phuket's high season (November–April), book 1–2 months ahead, especially for the small properties — Layalina (15 rooms) and PapaCrab (10 rooms) tend to fill first · In low season, 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty and rates drop substantially · Getting there: Kamala is about 45 minutes–1 hour from Phuket Airport by pre-booked taxi, hotel transfer or Grab · Every platform offers Free Cancellation rates — lock one in early if your plans might shift, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
